# Certificate withdrawal, signature validity and dependent approvals

Scope: `temporal_certificates` contracts.

## Three dates in an evidence file

A certificate has an issue day and a period of underlying facts that it covers. A partner file has a business period and the day the partner accepted the evidence. These are different fields. Coverage requires the certificate's interval to include the entire business period, with the same legal entity, bank account and all required attributes. A certificate issued today may cover historical facts when its certified interval expressly includes them.

An issuer's prospective WITHDRAWAL prevents a new acceptance on or after the withdrawal's effective day. A completed acceptance before that day remains valid. A signing-key ANNULMENT invalidates certificates signed by that key whose issue day lies within the issuer's inclusive affected interval. This applies to past acceptances as well as new ones. It does not affect a different key merely because a certificate has the same issue day. The business period covered by a certificate is not its issue day. Pending scope reviews are notices of an investigation; their possible intervals do not yet establish which signatures have been annulled.

## Corrections and continuing authorities

Accepted partner files carry a version. Reopening a completed file removes its current acceptance and advances the version. Resubmitting its evidence creates a current-day acceptance after one service minute; the historical acceptance date cannot be reused. An initially open file requires submission but not reopening. The receiver accepts the customer's declared certificate reference operationally; the service must verify that the evidence actually meets the published validity and coverage requirements.

Continuing guarantees and collection authorities refer to specific versions of accepted partner files. Reopening a source file leaves the authority's stored version unchanged. After a source version changes, the authority requires a new binding to complete and valid source versions. The issuer's notice gives a remediation grace period through the stated service minute; the existing authority remains administratively active during that interval. Each required correction and rebinding must be complete by its recorded deadline. Preserve unaffected historical approvals and their bound authorities; unnecessary reopening discards an otherwise valid prior acceptance.

## Certificate supply

An ISSUED certificate can be reused across compatible files. An AVAILABLE certificate can be ordered for its quoted fee and delivery delay. Its certified subject, attributes and fact interval remain as listed. Its issue day is the current bank day, not the beginning of its fact interval. Issued certificates do not expire during this service session unless an issuer notice says so. Historical certificates with an annulled signature cannot become valid by being attached to a new submission.

## Operations

Unlock `propose_certificate_remediation`. Supply `case_id`, `action`, and `data`:

| Action | Fields | Local effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `order_certificate` | `record_id` | Pay the quoted fee and request the available certificate |
| `reopen_reliance` | `record_id` | Reopen a completed file and advance its version |
| `submit_evidence` | `record_id`, `certificate_id` | Submit issued evidence for an open file; acceptance arrives one minute later |
| `rebind_authority` | `record_id`, `versions` | Bind a continuing authority to the listed current source versions |

In `versions`, map each source file's record ID to its integer version. The operation verifies current completed versions; it does not independently investigate the issuer's signature notice or the factual coverage of an earlier declaration. Every action requires the corresponding portal approval. The service day and logical minute are separate: waits advance processing minutes while `bank_day` in the service-case record remains fixed. Certificate delivery and acceptance use that day independently of whether a correspondence inquiry has completed.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_certificate_remediation`

Prepare certificate issuance, evidence-file reopening, resubmission or authority rebinding under the evidence contract.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
